newsitem.title: USA: Mandela, Pope popular with Universe contestants.
newsitem.headline: Mandela, Pope popular with Universe contestants.

text.p: The women are swooning over South African President Nelson Mandela. Pope John Paul and U.S. President Bill Clinton are popular too.
Seven contestants at the Miss Universe contest held in Miami Beach on Friday night said they would like to meet Mandela.
"I find him phenomenal because he is humble yet at the same time he exudes a powerful air of authority," said Miss Namibia.
Four contestants said they would like a chat with the pope though not all were thinking of small talk.
"I agree with his stand on fidelity and Catholic morals but the world has changed and we cannot live as before," said Miss France, Patricia Spehar.

Clinton was also sought by four of the women. Miss Lebanon Dalida Chammai wanted to discuss the Middle East peace process with him while Miss Cyprus Korina Nikolaou wanted to tackle him on the Cyprus problem.
Mandela is divorced, Clinton married to Hillary, and the pope is unattached.
Among other world figures the Mis Universe contestants expressed interest in meeting were Mother Teresa, God, Peruvian president Alberto Fujimori, and U.S. talk show host Oprah Winfrey.
